overreach: OFDM — Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing — is a modulation/multiplexing method where a wideband channel is split into many narrow, mutually orthogonal subcarriers.
Data is sent in parallel across those subcarriers, usually using QPSK/QAM symbols.
It is fundamental to systems such as LTE, 5G NR, Wi‑Fi, DVB, and many broadband radio links.
OFDM signals are structured in subcarriers, symbols, slots, resource blocks, numerologies, pilots/reference signals, etc.
If you need modulation quality, resource allocation, EVM, demodulation, or 5G/Wi‑Fi conformance insight, you need a standard-aware mode such as 5G NR/WLAN analysis rather than only spectrum mode.
OFDM has high occupied bandwidth, many subcarriers, and often high PAPR.
Choosing OBW, ACLR/spurious, and emission-mask style measurements correctly
In OFDM-based standards, test models define subcarrier/resource-block loading and signal structure, so the chosen test model affects the measurement result.
review.reason: The cited passages support that Spectrum vs 5G NR modes expose different measurements, that OBW and transmitter spurious emissions are Spectrum-mode measurements, that PRS must not overlap SSB OFDM symbols, and that Tx ON/OFF setup includes selecting a test model, power unit, and noise cancellation. However, the OFDM definition and several asserted measurement implications such as EVM/demodulation, WLAN/DVB modes, ACLR/emission-mask, PAPR, and test-model resource-block loading are not supported by the cited passages, even though some are partly disclaimed as general knowledge.
